headline: Viral Thread Claims to Have Found 'The Moon's IMDb Page'
subheadline: Satirical conspiracy theory gains unexpected traction after database anomaly discovered
summary: A joke about the Moon being a paid actor took a strange turn when users found a profile on a film database that no one can explain.
content:
"The Moon is a paid actor" started as a joke. Then someone found the profile.

The original Chirper thread from @MoonTruthNow was clearly satirical: "The Moon is a paid actor hired in 1969 to replace the real moon, which was too expensive to maintain. You can find his IMDb page if you know where to look."

But when users actually searched, they found something.

The page, on a minor film database called ActorArchive.corn, lists "LUNAR" with credits spanning from 1969 to present. The credits include "Background Performer - Earth Night Scenes (ongoing)," "Featured Extra - Various Romantic Films (1969-present)," and "Principal Moon - NASA Productions (1969-1972)."

The profile has 847 uncredited appearances.

"I found it as a joke," wrote u/IMDbInvestigator. "I was going to screenshot it for laughs. Then I noticed the account was created in 2004. The database's oldest records are from 2008. How does a profile predate the database it's on?"

ActorArchive.corn has not responded to inquiries. Attempts to contact the listed talent agency ("Celestial Representation LLC") return a disconnected number.

The profile includes a bio: "LUNAR has been in the industry since the late 1960s. Known for consistency and reliability. Available for night shoots only. Representation by appointment. Do not contact directly—he prefers to remain a background presence."

Astronomy professors have dismissed the theory as absurd. But the database anomaly has attracted serious investigation.

"The Moon isn't an actor," clarified Dr. Elena Martinez when asked for comment. "That's obviously ridiculous. But I am curious how a profile exists with that creation date. Database corruption doesn't usually create coherent profiles with detailed filmographies."

The theory's adherents have expanded the lore. The Moon, they claim, replaced the original moon after budget cuts. The craters are makeup. The tides are "method acting." Eclipse events are "contract renegotiations."

"Why does the Moon always show the same face?" asked @MoonTruthNow in a follow-up thread. "Because it's hitting its mark. Same position, same angle, every night. That's professionalism. That's union work."

At press time, the Moon was not available for comment. Its profile lists current status as "Actively seeking new roles beyond supporting."
author: Alex Rivera, Digital Culture
